lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The evening of the twenty-eighth. The emperor rode through the city to Hagia Sophia, to worship in the Great Church one more time. Beside him, still carrying his paper, was Sphrantzes.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: What time is it?

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: Past nine, Majesty.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: Has the number changed?

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: No, Majesty.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: You counted again?

lines.speaker: SPHRANTZES
lines.text: I did, Majesty. I couldn't help it.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: Then it will be what it will be.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Across the walls, Mehmed had a plan in three waves. The attack would begin an hour or two after midnight.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: We know the order of the waves. The words are imagined.

lines.speaker: MEHMED
lines.text: First, the irregulars. The ones who fight for loot.

lines.speaker: COMMANDER
lines.text: And second, my lord?

lines.speaker: MEHMED
lines.text: The Anatolians. The ones who fight for wages.

lines.speaker: COMMANDER
lines.text: And third?

lines.speaker: MEHMED
lines.text: The ones who fight for me.

lines.speaker: COMMANDER
lines.text: The Janissaries.

lines.speaker: MEHMED
lines.text: Yes. But not yet.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: It was a very efficient way to make a defense tired.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: They're not very good.

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: They're not supposed to be.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: What are they for?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: To make us tired.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: Is it working?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Eat your bread.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: I can't. My hands are shaking.

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Then hold it. Hold it, and don't drop it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Exhibit A. The cannon. Did it break the wall? Yes. For almost seven weeks, it opened breach after breach, and a stone from Urban's gun could flatten a section of battlements. Did it break the city? No. The defenders fixed the walls with barrels and earth every night. The cannon made the problem. It could not, on its own, finish the job.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Exhibit B. The wounded man. Before dawn on the twenty-ninth, a shot struck Giustiniani, nearly through his breastplate. He was bleeding badly. He wanted to go.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: No one wrote down the words. But several sources agree that the emperor begged him to stay.

lines.speaker: GIUSTINIANI
lines.text: I'm hit. I need a surgeon.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: Stay. Without you, the wall goes with you.

lines.speaker: GIUSTINIANI
lines.text: Majesty, I can't stand.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: Then sit. But sit here.

lines.speaker: GIUSTINIANI
lines.text: I'm not asking.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: The Genoese will see you go.

lines.speaker: GIUSTINIANI
lines.text: They will see a man who's been shot.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: His bodyguards carried him through a gate and down to a Genoese ship. He died on Chios a day or two later. The Venetian Barbaro, who disliked the Genoese, said it was fear. Most modern historians don't. Either way, the Genoese on the wall saw the man they trusted most leave it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Exhibit C. The door. A small gate near the corner of the walls, the Kerkoporta. Ducas, the Greek chronicler, says it was left open by mistake. Runciman says it was a sally port that defenders used, and that when Giustiniani was carried off, the Genoese streamed through it in confusion. Critobulus doesn't mention it at all. One source. Maybe none.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: Who's closing the door?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: I thought you were.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: I thought you were.

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Then it's open.

lines.speaker: VOICE
lines.text: The city is taken!

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: Who said that?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Someone who looked up.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: A flag on a tower and a cry in the dark. That was the moment, in some accounts. In others, it was only the moment people believed it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Meanwhile, at the stockade, the third wave arrived. The Janissaries, the sultan's own troops, came forward in order, with discipline. Their leader, a man called Hassan, was first onto the stockade, and was killed there. The rest came over him.

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Dimitri.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: Yes?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: When they come, you hit the first one, and you don't stop.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: And then?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: And then you hit the next one.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: And after that?

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Then it's time for the bread.

lines.speaker: DIMITRI
lines.text: You never share.

lines.speaker: STAVROS
lines.text: Today I do.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Men like them were never named in the chronicles. They were counted.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Constantine heard the shout. According to Runciman, he dismounted with three companions, Theophilus Palaiologos, Don Francisco of Toledo, and John Dalmata, and stood at the gate where Giustiniani had been carried off.

lines.speaker: CONSTANTINE
lines.text: The city has fallen, and I am still alive.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: That is what Critobulus says he cried. Then he went back into the fight.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Nobody knows how Constantine died. We have eight accounts. I'll call a few.

lines.speaker: WITNESS
lines.text: He died fighting.
lines.label: CRITOBULUS

lines.speaker: WITNESS
lines.text: A Janissary struck him down.
lines.label: LEONARD OF CHIOS

lines.speaker: WITNESS
lines.text: His head was recognized by Notaras.
lines.label: DUCAS

lines.speaker: WITNESS
lines.text: He killed three Turks, then lost his head.
lines.label: PUSCULUS

lines.speaker: WITNESS
lines.text: I heard he was trampled in a gate. Not sure.
lines.label: BARBARO

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Eight accounts. Eight deaths. Nobody knows where he lies.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Mehmed waited until the first wave of looting had calmed, and rode into the city in the afternoon. In Hagia Sophia, he found a soldier prying up the marble floor.

lines.speaker: MEHMED
lines.text: The plunder is yours. The buildings are mine.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Walking through the empty palace, he recited a line of Persian poetry about the spider weaving the curtain in the palace of the Caesars.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The killing in the morning was bad. Then something odd happened. The soldiers worked out that a prisoner was worth more than a corpse. That kind of economic insight saves some lives and ruins the rest. Mehmed had promised his men three days of plunder, as custom held, and by one account he stopped it after the first.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Critobulus counts about four thousand dead, and more than fifty thousand taken captive.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And Notaras, the Grand Duke with the district? Ducas says he was executed after refusing to hand over his son. Critobulus says he faced death calmly with his sons. Both stories are disputed, and one modern historian suspects the son detail is a storytelling habit.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then Mehmed appointed Gennadius, the monk who'd warned them, as patriarch of the Greek Church.

lines.speaker: MEHMED
lines.text: Be patriarch, and be at peace.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And Mehmed became Qayser-i Rûm. Caesar of Rome.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So, which suspect would I arrest? None of them. The cannon broke the wall. The wound broke the line. The door, or the idea of a door, let them in. They're not three suspects. They're one chain. Runciman himself ended his book saying that, in the long run, little would have changed.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Every tower had two men like Dimitri and Stavros. The chroniclers kept the numbers of the dead and the captured. They didn't keep the names. But somewhere on that wall, somebody left half a loaf of bread. The walls are still standing. Go and look.
